- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The 50mm focal length is considered a classic portrait lens, and a prime lens helps create a shallow depth of field.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bokeh refers to the aesthetic quality of the blur produced in the out-of-focus parts of an image.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] General tips for taking better portrait photos include understanding camera settings, paying attention to lighting, working with the subject, focusing on the eyes, and experimenting with composition.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For outdoor portraits, use a wide aperture (like f/1.8 or f/2.8) and shoot during the golden hour for warm, soft light.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For indoor portraits, use a slightly narrower aperture (like f/2.2 or f/3.2) and consider using artificial light sources.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] For low-light portraits, use a wide aperture (like f/1.8 or f/2.8) and a higher ISO (like 1600 or 3200).

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for utilizing burst mode for portrait photography include anticipating the moment, using burst mode for candid moments, focusing on the eyes, adjusting burst mode settings, and being mindful of buffer capacity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] When using burst mode, review and select the best shots, practice timing, and consider using continuous autofocus.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Don't overdo burst mode; curate the best images during editing.
